explanation: The right phrenic nerve accompanies the inferior vena cava through the central tendon at T8. The left phrenic nerve usually pierces the muscular diaphragm separately.
The plantar calcaneonavicular ligament, also called the spring ligament, supports the head of the talus and helps maintain the medial longitudinal arch.
Sebaceous glands release their product by disintegration of the entire secretory cell. This is holocrine secretion, unlike secretion by exocytosis.
The abducens nerve passes through Dorello's canal beneath the petrosphenoidal ligament before entering the cavernous sinus. This course makes it vulnerable to stretch.
The genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve supplies cremaster and forms the efferent limb. Sensory input is carried chiefly through the ilioinguinal nerve.
Gastrointestinal stromal tumours arise from the interstitial-cell-of-Cajal lineage. These pacemaker-related cells differ from ordinary gastrointestinal smooth muscle cells.
Surfactant reduces surface tension at the alveolar air-fluid interface. This lowers the work needed to expand the lung and limits small-alveolus collapse.
Glycogen phosphorylase uses pyridoxal phosphate, a vitamin B6 derivative. The reaction releases glucose-1-phosphate from glycogen by phosphorolysis.
Type I collagen predominates in bone, tendon and ligament. Most cartilage instead contains type II collagen; fibrocartilage is an important exception to that generalisation.
The inferior thyroid artery usually arises from the thyrocervical trunk of the subclavian artery. The superior thyroid artery usually arises from the external carotid.
A rise in arterial pressure increases baroreceptor firing and triggers responses that lower pressure. Because the response opposes the initial change, this is negative feedback.
The thick ascending limb reabsorbs sodium, potassium and chloride while remaining poorly permeable to water. Solute removal therefore dilutes tubular fluid.
Humans lack functional L-gulonolactone oxidase, needed for the final step of ascorbate synthesis. Vitamin C must therefore be obtained from the diet.
The Klenow fragment retains DNA polymerase I polymerase and proofreading functions but lacks its 5-prime-to-3-prime exonuclease domain. It can extend DNA without that nuclease activity.
Reverse transcription converts RNA into complementary DNA, which PCR then amplifies. Conventional PCR directly amplifies DNA rather than RNA.
Ascorbate promotes non-haem iron absorption by maintaining iron in its more soluble ferrous form and helping keep it available for intestinal uptake.
Inversion occurs chiefly at the subtalar and transverse tarsal joints. Talocalcaneal is another name for the subtalar joint; the talocrural joint mainly permits dorsiflexion and plantarflexion.
The right superior intercostal vein usually drains upper posterior intercostal spaces into the azygos vein. The left counterpart usually drains to the left brachiocephalic vein.
Temporalis, masseter and medial pterygoid elevate the mandible. Lateral pterygoid contributes to protrusion and opening rather than acting as a primary jaw elevator.
The articular disc separates the distal ulna from the carpal bones. The radiocarpal articulation involves the distal radius and disc proximally, with proximal-row carpals distally.
In a polarised serous acinar cell, the Golgi apparatus occupies the supranuclear region. It processes secretory proteins before they are packaged toward the apical surface.
Meissner corpuscles lie in dermal papillae of glabrous skin. They are rapidly adapting mechanoreceptors involved in light touch and low-frequency vibration.
Submandibular nodes form level IB. Submental nodes are level IA; both belong to the level I group used in cervical lymph-node classification.
Hypothalamic dopamine tonically inhibits prolactin release from pituitary lactotrophs. Milk production is promoted by prolactin, whereas milk ejection is chiefly mediated by oxytocin.
The second and third dorsal interossei insert on opposite sides of the middle finger. They abduct the middle finger in either direction from its axial position.
The anterior ethmoidal artery arises from the ophthalmic artery of the internal carotid system. The other listed septal contributors belong to the external carotid system.
The common carotid usually bifurcates near the upper border of the thyroid cartilage, around C4. Its exact level varies between individuals.
Golgi tendon organs sense muscle tension through Ib afferent fibres. Muscle spindles instead provide information about muscle length and its rate of change.
The pre-Botzinger complex in the ventrolateral medulla is a key component of the respiratory rhythm-generating network. Other respiratory centres modify and coordinate its activity.
The adrenal zona reticularis secretes androgen precursors, notably DHEA and DHEA sulfate. Peripheral tissues can convert these precursors into more potent sex steroids.
Heme synthesis begins with condensation of glycine and succinyl-CoA to form aminolevulinate. Succinyl-CoA links this pathway with the citric acid cycle.
Urothelium lines the renal collecting system and ureter. The membranous urethra is chiefly lined by pseudostratified or stratified columnar epithelium rather than typical urothelium.
Sternocleidomastoid is enclosed by the investing layer of deep cervical fascia. The pretracheal fascial compartment surrounds cervical viscera including thyroid, trachea and oesophagus.
Most superior cerebellar peduncle efferent fibres cross in the caudal midbrain at the level of the inferior colliculi, before reaching their contralateral targets.
The pancreas lacks striated ducts, whereas salivary glands such as the parotid have them. Centroacinar cells are another useful feature of exocrine pancreas.
Hepatic stellate cells, also called Ito cells, occupy the space of Disse. They store vitamin A and can become collagen-producing cells during liver injury.
Corticospinal fibres run in the posterior limb of the internal capsule. A lesion above the pyramidal decussation can therefore produce weakness on the opposite side.
Type IV hypersensitivity is mediated by sensitised T cells and their recruited effector cells. It is delayed and does not depend primarily on circulating antibodies.
HMG-CoA lyase cleaves HMG-CoA during ketone-body synthesis. Cholesterol synthesis instead uses HMG-CoA reductase to produce mevalonate.
The superior cerebellar peduncles decussate in the caudal midbrain. Their crossing is separate from the sensory and pyramidal decussations of the medulla.
The cervical sympathetic trunk lies posterior to the carotid sheath. The sheath contains the carotid artery, internal jugular vein and vagus nerve.
Normal somatic cells have a limited replicative lifespan before senescence. Telomere shortening is a major contributor; telomerase can extend this lifespan in some cell types.
PCR first separates DNA strands by denaturation, then allows primers to anneal, and finally extends them with DNA polymerase. Repeated cycles amplify the target sequence.
Protein generally has a greater thermic effect than carbohydrate or fat. Digestion, amino-acid processing and protein turnover contribute to this energy expenditure.
Vitamin D3 is generated in skin, converted to 25-hydroxyvitamin D mainly in liver, and then activated to calcitriol primarily by the kidney.
Delayed hypersensitivity is driven by T-cell responses, including cytokine-mediated inflammation and direct cytotoxicity. This distinguishes it from antibody-mediated hypersensitivity mechanisms.
Tetanic stimulation at 50 Hz is a standard pattern used in neuromuscular monitoring. Interpretation depends on the stimulation protocol and the degree of neuromuscular blockade.
RNA interference reduces gene expression by targeting messenger RNA for degradation or translational repression. This is knockdown rather than permanent removal of the underlying gene.
Insulin suppresses hormone-sensitive lipase activity in adipose tissue, reducing mobilisation of stored triglyceride. Lipoprotein lipase serves a different role in clearing circulating triglycerides.
Mature red blood cells lack mitochondria and depend on glucose metabolism for energy. They cannot use fatty-acid oxidation or ketone-body oxidation to generate ATP.
Posterior urethral valves are a major congenital cause of bladder outlet obstruction in boys. Obstruction may damage the bladder and upper urinary tract.
Vitamin C deficiency impairs hydroxylation of proline and lysine during collagen formation. This weakens connective tissue and contributes to the bleeding and poor wound healing of scurvy.
Pyruvate dehydrogenase requires thiamine pyrophosphate. Reduced conversion of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA can divert pyruvate toward lactate and contribute to lactic acidosis.
Vitamin B12 is needed by methionine synthase to transfer a methyl group from methyl-tetrahydrofolate. Deficiency traps folate in that form and impairs nucleotide synthesis.
An RNA target must first be reverse-transcribed into complementary DNA before PCR amplification. This is the principle of reverse-transcription PCR.
Acetyl-CoA does not provide net glucose in humans because its carbons are lost during the citric acid cycle. Glycerol, lactate and glucogenic amino acids can supply gluconeogenesis.
Flexible pairing at the third codon position allows one tRNA to recognise more than one synonymous codon. This helps explain degeneracy of the genetic code.
Triglycerides lack the prominent polar head group found in phospholipids and glycolipids. They are predominantly hydrophobic storage lipids rather than amphipathic membrane lipids.
Local anaesthetics reversibly block voltage-gated sodium channels and prevent action-potential propagation. Their action depends partly on channel state and membrane access.
Parvovirus B19 infects erythroid precursors and temporarily suppresses red-cell production. In a patient with chronic haemolysis, this can produce a transient aplastic crisis.
A normal adult prostate is approximately 20 mL, although size varies with age and measurement method. Enlargement alone does not determine whether disease is benign or malignant.
The Lisfranc ligament connects the medial cuneiform to the base of the second metatarsal. It stabilises the tarsometatarsal complex and is central to Lisfranc injuries.
Maple syrup urine disease impairs breakdown of branched-chain amino acids: leucine, isoleucine and valine. Methionine is not a branched-chain amino acid.
Somatic hypermutation generates immunoglobulin-variable-region variants in germinal centres. Selection of B cells with better antigen binding produces affinity maturation.
Deamination of 5-methylcytosine produces thymine rather than uracil. If unrepaired, the resulting mismatch can become a C-to-T transition mutation.
MHC class I displays intracellularly derived peptides to CD8-positive cytotoxic T cells. MHC class II usually presents extracellularly derived peptides to CD4-positive helper T cells.
Protein has the largest thermic effect among the major dietary macronutrients. Processing amino acids and changing protein turnover require more energy than processing an equivalent fat intake.
The banana sign reflects an abnormally curved cerebellum associated with Chiari II malformation and open spina bifida. It is an ultrasound sign rather than a separate disease.
Molybdenum is a cofactor for xanthine oxidoreductase. Deficiency can impair conversion of xanthine to uric acid and increase urinary xanthine.
Pompe disease results from deficient lysosomal acid alpha-glucosidase. Glycogen accumulates within lysosomes, with prominent muscle and, in infantile disease, cardiac involvement.
Pyridoxal phosphate is required in tryptophan metabolism. Vitamin B6 deficiency can divert metabolites toward xanthurenic acid, increasing its urinary excretion.
The Mount Fuji sign describes separation and compression of the frontal lobes by subdural air. In the appropriate clinical setting it supports tension pneumocephalus.
Water defines zero Hounsfield units on the CT attenuation scale. Air is approximately minus 1000 HU, while dense bone has a strongly positive value.
Veraguth folds are classically described in depression. Allergic shiners, the allergic salute and Dennie-Morgan folds are associated with allergic rhinitis or atopy.
The Downes score grades neonatal respiratory distress using respiratory rate, cyanosis, air entry, grunting and retractions. It assesses severity rather than establishing one specific cause.
The hepatocystic triangle is bounded by the cystic duct, common hepatic duct and inferior surface of the liver. The cystic artery usually runs within it.
Many cancer cells show increased glycolysis with lactate production despite available oxygen. This aerobic glycolysis is called the Warburg effect and supports biosynthetic demands.
Tight junctions occupy the apicolateral region of epithelial cells. They restrict paracellular movement and help maintain distinct apical and basolateral membrane domains.
Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma is highly vascular. Routine diagnostic biopsy risks severe haemorrhage; assessment relies on the clinical pattern and appropriate imaging.
The ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve supplies most orbital sensation. The optic nerve carries vision, and ocular motor nerves chiefly supply extraocular muscles.
Reduced renal perfusion stimulates renin release from juxtaglomerular cells. Low macula-densa sodium-chloride delivery and beta1-adrenergic stimulation can also promote renin release.
Beta-adrenergic receptors couple mainly to Gs and stimulate adenylyl cyclase. Alpha1 receptors use Gq, while alpha2 and M2 receptors couple mainly to Gi.
Light reduces cyclic-GMP-mediated cation entry into photoreceptors and hyperpolarises them. This differs from many sensory receptors, which depolarise when stimulated.
The loop of Henle generates the medullary osmotic gradient by countercurrent multiplication. Active salt transport in its water-impermeable thick ascending limb is essential to this process.
Insulin promotes GLUT4 translocation in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue. Hepatic glucose transport mainly uses GLUT2 and does not depend on insulin-triggered GLUT4 recruitment.

SGLT1 couples sodium and glucose uptake in the small intestine. Water follows solute absorption, explaining why glucose-containing oral rehydration solution remains effective during many diarrhoeal illnesses.
Pyridoxal phosphate, derived from vitamin B6, is the coenzyme used by aminotransferases. It temporarily carries amino groups during transamination reactions.
Sucrose is non-reducing because both anomeric carbons participate in its glycosidic bond. Glucose and fructose can give positive Benedict reactions under the test conditions.
The urinary bladder lies behind the pubic symphysis and can rise into the lower anterior abdomen when distended. The aorta, renal vein and spinal cord occupy more posterior or superior positions.
Koch's triangle is bounded by the tendon of Todaro, the septal tricuspid annulus and the coronary sinus ostium. The atrioventricular node lies near its apex.

An uncomplicated isolated atrial septal defect produces a low-pressure shunt and has a relatively low endocarditis risk. High-velocity jets and abnormal valves promote endothelial injury and vegetation formation.
Elimination half-life helps estimate how rapidly drug concentration falls and informs the dosing interval. It does not by itself establish drug potency, clinical efficacy or toxicity thresholds.
HPV16 is a high-risk oncogenic type associated with cervical cancer. HPV6 and HPV11 are usually low-risk types associated with anogenital warts.
Gonioscopy uses a contact lens to overcome total internal reflection and visualise the anterior chamber angle. It helps distinguish open-angle from angle-closure mechanisms.
A Littre hernia contains a Meckel diverticulum within the hernia sac. A Richter hernia instead traps only part of the bowel circumference.
The subclavian vein passes anterior to anterior scalene, while the artery passes posterior to it. The phrenic nerve descends on the anterior surface of the muscle.
The superior gluteal nerve supplies gluteus medius, gluteus minimus and tensor fasciae latae. Gluteus maximus is supplied by the inferior gluteal nerve.
The greater petrosal nerve carries preganglionic parasympathetic fibres toward the pterygopalatine ganglion. Postganglionic fibres then reach the lacrimal gland through trigeminal branches.
The thoracodorsal nerve supplies latissimus dorsi, which extends, adducts and medially rotates the humerus. The nerve is vulnerable during axillary surgery.
Cervical transverse processes contain transverse foramina. The vertebral artery normally passes through those of C6 to C1, whereas the C7 foramen commonly carries veins.
The occipital lobe forms part of the cerebral hemispheres and contains primary visual cortex. The hypothalamus belongs to the diencephalon, while the medulla belongs to the brainstem.
Cricoid is the only complete cartilaginous ring of the larynx. Its broad posterior lamina and narrow anterior arch lie below the thyroid cartilage.
Hair follicles and cutaneous glandular epithelia arise from surface ectoderm. Arrector pili are smooth muscles derived from mesenchyme.
The iris dilator and sphincter muscles develop from neuroectoderm of the optic cup. This makes them exceptions to the predominantly mesodermal origin of muscle.
The buccopharyngeal membrane consists of apposed ectoderm and endoderm without intervening mesoderm. Its breakdown establishes the early opening between the stomodeum and foregut.
Tympanometry assesses middle-ear pressure and compliance and can support evaluation of Eustachian tube dysfunction. VEMP assesses vestibular pathways, while rhinomanometry assesses nasal airflow.
Nitrous oxide rapidly diffuses from blood into alveoli when administration stops, transiently diluting alveolar oxygen. Supplemental oxygen limits this diffusion hypoxia.
Pyruvate carboxylase forms oxaloacetate from pyruvate, replenishing a citric-acid-cycle intermediate. Reactions that refill the cycle are called anaplerotic.
A low insulin-to-glucagon ratio promotes fat mobilisation, hepatic fatty-acid oxidation and ketone-body synthesis. It suppresses anabolic storage pathways characteristic of the fed state.
Protein has a relatively high energy cost for digestion, amino-acid processing and metabolic turnover. Its thermic effect is therefore generally greater than that of fat or carbohydrate.
The superficial fibular nerve supplies fibularis longus and brevis in the lateral compartment. Fibularis tertius and extensor hallucis longus receive the deep fibular nerve.
Repair of a cleft lip includes reconstruction of the interrupted orbicularis oris muscle. Restoring its continuity helps recover oral sphincter function.
The deep ulnar branch supplies most intrinsic hand muscles, including the third lumbrical, opponens digiti minimi and dorsal interossei. Flexor carpi ulnaris receives a branch in the forearm.
Insulin normally recruits GLUT4 to the surface of skeletal muscle cells. Impaired insulin signalling reduces this glucose uptake; brain and red cells primarily use insulin-independent transporters.

Glycogen debranching-enzyme deficiency produces glycogen storage disease type III with abnormal limit-dextrin accumulation. Some response to glucagon may persist after feeding, while prolonged fasting exhausts accessible glycogen.
Prolonged topical corticosteroid exposure can cause skin atrophy, acneiform eruptions and hypertrichosis. Risk increases with potency, duration, occlusion and use on thin skin.

A preceding genital ulcer followed by a palmoplantar eruption raises suspicion of secondary syphilis. Serologic testing supports diagnosis; interpretation combines treponemal and nontreponemal tests with the clinical context.
Trismus with painful muscle spasms after an ear infection suggests otogenic tetanus. Tetanospasmin blocks release of inhibitory neurotransmitters, producing sustained muscle rigidity and spasms.
Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma is a highly vascular tumour associated with nasal obstruction and recurrent epistaxis in adolescent males. Routine office biopsy can provoke severe bleeding.
Brief episodes of vertigo triggered by rolling in bed suggest benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Displaced otoconia stimulate a semicircular canal during particular head movements.
The internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve lies close to the piriform recess mucosa. A sharp foreign body can injure it and affect sensation above the vocal folds.
Aluminium phosphide releases phosphine on contact with moisture or acid. Phosphine can reduce silver nitrate to metallic silver, causing blackening in a screening test.

Chronic mercury exposure can cause intention tremor and neuropsychiatric change, traditionally described as erethism or mad-hatter syndrome. Basophilic stippling and metaphyseal lead lines instead suggest lead exposure.
Candida oesophagitis is associated with odynophagia and adherent white plaques in immunocompromised patients. Microscopy can show budding yeast and pseudohyphae.
The Kanagawa phenomenon is beta-haemolysis on Wagatsuma agar associated with thermostable direct haemolysin-producing Vibrio parahaemolyticus strains.
Cryptococcus is an encapsulated yeast rather than a classic thermally dimorphic fungus. Histoplasma, Coccidioides and Talaromyces marneffei are conventionally grouped with dimorphic fungi.

Strongyloides larvae can become infective within the host and penetrate intestinal or perianal tissue. This autoinfection cycle permits persistent infection and can accelerate during immunosuppression.
Toxoplasma gondii is an obligate intracellular parasite. Laboratory propagation can use cell culture or inoculation of susceptible mice; ordinary bacteriologic agar does not support its growth.

The Rotterdam approach requires two of ovulatory dysfunction, hyperandrogenism and polycystic ovarian morphology after excluding alternatives. In the listed choices, delayed cycles and hirsutism represent the first two features.
High-risk HPV types 16 and 18 account for a large proportion of cervical cancers. Types 6 and 11 are mainly associated with anogenital warts.
Maternal fever more commonly produces fetal tachycardia. Head compression, severe placental compromise and congenital heart block can produce slower fetal heart rates.
Positioning precedes speculum insertion. Once the cervix is visualised, a suitable sampling device can collect cervical cells; specimen collection should follow the relevant screening protocol.
Osteosarcoma can produce an aggressive periosteal reaction, including a sunburst pattern and a Codman triangle. These signs require interpretation alongside the site and other imaging findings.
Rheumatoid inflammation can weaken stabilising ligaments around the odontoid and cause atlantoaxial instability. Cervical pain with myelopathic signs warrants evaluation for cord compromise.
The Honda or H-shaped sacral pattern reflects bilateral vertical sacral insufficiency fractures with a connecting transverse component. MRI can show the associated marrow oedema.
Armanni-Ebstein change is glycogen accumulation in renal tubular epithelium. Mesangial expansion, basement-membrane thickening and podocyte loss are glomerular changes of diabetic kidney disease.
Mucosal neuromas characterise MEN2B, which is associated with activating RET variants. TP53 is associated with Li-Fraumeni syndrome rather than being the defining MEN2B gene.
Von Willebrand disease is the most common inherited bleeding disorder. Deficient or dysfunctional von Willebrand factor impairs platelet adhesion and can reduce factor VIII stability.
Turner syndrome commonly includes short stature, a webbed neck, a broad chest and short fourth metacarpals. A prominent occiput is classically associated with Edwards syndrome.
Bloom syndrome is an autosomal recessive DNA-repair disorder involving BLM. Trisomies and the extra sex chromosome in Klinefelter syndrome are numerical chromosome abnormalities.
Inflammasome activation can activate caspase-1, leading to gasdermin-mediated membrane pores and inflammatory pyroptotic cell death. This differs from conventional noninflammatory apoptosis.

Thalidomide has immunomodulatory effects and is used in selected myeloma and erythema nodosum leprosum regimens. Its severe teratogenicity requires strict pregnancy-prevention safeguards; it is not a conventional antimetabolite.

Both drug groups enhance GABA-mediated inhibition and can add to alcohol-induced sedation. Flumazenil antagonises benzodiazepine-site effects, while thiopentone initially wears off mainly through redistribution rather than metabolism.
Phase I metabolism includes oxidation, reduction and hydrolysis. These reactions introduce or expose functional groups, sometimes enabling subsequent phase II conjugation.
Posterior alpha activity is most evident during relaxed wakefulness with the eyes closed. Eye opening attenuates this rhythm, a response called alpha blocking.
Tight junctions occupy the apical part of the lateral membrane in epithelial cells. They form a paracellular barrier and help preserve apical-basolateral polarity.
Fever involves an increased thermoregulatory set point mediated chiefly through prostaglandin E2 signalling in the preoptic hypothalamic region.
Acute altitude exposure stimulates ventilation because inspired oxygen pressure falls. Increased carbon-dioxide loss produces respiratory alkalosis before renal compensation develops.
Using the simplified examination relation, frequency is the reciprocal of contraction time. One divided by 0.040 seconds is 25 hertz; physiological fusion thresholds vary with muscle properties.
Mean and median describe central tendency rather than dispersion. Measures such as variance, standard deviation and interquartile range describe spread.
Quantiles locate observations within an ordered distribution. Quartiles divide it into four parts and tertiles into three; neither is itself a single measure of central tendency.
A study begins with a research question and defined objectives. Population selection and study procedures follow, with analysis performed after data collection.

Valproate exposure during pregnancy is associated with neural-tube defects and adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes. Pregnancy planning requires specialist medication review rather than abrupt unsupervised discontinuation.

The hippocampal formation is central to formation and consolidation of declarative or explicit memories. Procedural motor learning relies more on other circuits, including the basal ganglia and cerebellum.

Ketamine can produce a rapid antidepressant response through mechanisms involving NMDA-receptor antagonism and downstream glutamatergic signalling. Clinical use requires appropriate supervised assessment and monitoring.
Lithium, valproate and antipsychotics such as haloperidol can be used in acute mania depending on the clinical setting. Amitriptyline is an antidepressant and may worsen mood switching.

Technetium-99m sestamibi imaging can help localise hyperfunctioning parathyroid tissue before surgery. Imaging localises a lesion; biochemical evaluation establishes the diagnosis of hyperparathyroidism.

An eye-of-the-tiger appearance in the globus pallidus is classically associated with pantothenate kinase-associated neurodegeneration. The pattern reflects central signal change within surrounding iron-associated low signal.
Intramucosal colorectal carcinoma is classified as Tis. In the absence of nodal or distant disease this corresponds to stage 0 rather than an invasive stage I tumour.
Urinary citrate binds calcium and inhibits crystal formation. Low citrate promotes calcium stones; increased urinary calcium, oxalate or uric acid can also promote stone formation.
Noncontrast CT of the urinary tract is highly sensitive for ureteric calculi in nonpregnant adults. Ultrasound may be preferred initially where radiation avoidance is particularly important.
The Los Angeles system grades erosive oesophagitis. Achalasia is classified using manometric patterns, conventionally described with the Chicago classification.
Excess iodine can increase thyroid hormone synthesis in susceptible autonomous thyroid tissue. This iodine-induced hyperthyroidism is called the Jod-Basedow phenomenon.
Volume depletion can stimulate antidiuretic hormone despite low plasma osmolality. Water retention, particularly with hypotonic fluid intake, can then contribute to hyponatraemia.
Helicobacter-associated ulcer risk depends on bacterial virulence, host susceptibility and environmental factors. Infection therefore does not produce peptic ulceration in every infected individual.
MMR contains live attenuated viruses and is contraindicated in severe cellular immunodeficiency. Inactivated vaccines do not carry the same replication risk, although immune responses may be reduced.
Tetralogy of Fallot includes right-ventricular outflow obstruction, a ventricular septal defect, an overriding aorta and right-ventricular hypertrophy. The obstruction is often infundibular.
Carbohydrate refeeding increases insulin, shifting phosphate, potassium and magnesium into cells. This can cause dangerous electrolyte depletion in a malnourished patient.
Proliferative diabetic retinopathy can form fibrovascular membranes that contract and pull the retina away from the underlying tissue. This produces tractional retinal detachment.
Optical coherence tomography provides high-resolution cross-sectional images of retinal layers. Perimetry assesses visual fields rather than retinal microanatomy.
Mebendazole interferes with helminth microtubules and glucose utilisation. It is used against several intestinal nematodes, whereas amoebiasis requires an antiamoebic regimen.
Toxocara larvae can migrate through human tissues after ingestion of infective eggs. Humans are accidental hosts and do not complete the normal intestinal adult-worm cycle.
Wheat protein is relatively deficient in lysine compared with reference amino-acid requirements. Combining cereal and pulse proteins can improve the overall amino-acid pattern.
Kienbock disease is osteonecrosis of the lunate. The other eponyms refer to different bones, including the femoral head in Perthes disease.

Stylopharyngeus is supplied by the glossopharyngeal nerve. Most other pharyngeal muscles receive vagal motor supply through the pharyngeal plexus; older descriptions attributed these fibres to the cranial accessory component.
Within the traditional examination model, CSF absorption increases as CSF pressure rises relative to venous pressure. This pressure-dependent outflow is an important regulator of CSF pressure.
Low plasma osmolality normally suppresses ADH secretion. Pain, nausea or substantial volume depletion can provide nonosmotic stimuli that modify the normal osmotic response.
Branches of the vertebral, anterior spinal and posterior inferior cerebellar arteries supply the medulla. The superior cerebellar artery primarily supplies superior cerebellar structures.
Stylohyoid receives facial-nerve motor supply. The pterygoids and tensor veli palatini are supplied by mandibular-division branches of the trigeminal nerve.
Parotid parasympathetic fibres originate in the glossopharyngeal pathway and synapse in the otic ganglion. Facial-nerve pathways supply the other listed glands.
Repeated hair pulling can produce broken shafts at different lengths, perifollicular injury and nonscarring alopecia. These findings favour trichotillomania over uniform patterned hair loss.

Persistent gallbladder nonvisualisation under an appropriate hepatobiliary scintigraphy protocol can indicate cystic-duct obstruction in acute cholecystitis. Fasting, hepatic dysfunction and other factors can affect interpretation.
Phenylbutyrate is converted to phenylacetate, which conjugates with glutamine. Urinary excretion of phenylacetylglutamine provides an alternative route for nitrogen disposal.
A low insulin-to-glucagon ratio characterises fasting and promotes fuel mobilisation. Glycogen synthesis and storage are favoured instead by the insulin-dominant fed state.
CRISPR-Cas9 uses a guide RNA to direct a nuclease to a chosen DNA sequence. Association studies identify correlations, while microscopy and diagnostic amplification have different purposes.
Serotonin can activate cardiac vagal afferents, including through 5-HT3 receptors, and evoke the Bezold-Jarisch reflex with bradycardia and hypotension.

At the hilum, the pulmonary veins are generally anterior, with pulmonary arterial structures between the veins and the more posterior bronchi. Superior-inferior arrangements differ between the two sides.
The mental artery is a terminal branch of the inferior alveolar artery. The labial and lateral nasal arteries are branches of the facial artery.
The superior gluteal nerve supplies gluteus medius, gluteus minimus and tensor fasciae latae. Piriformis receives separate branches from the sacral plexus.
ATP binding lowers the affinity of myosin for actin and permits detachment. ATP hydrolysis then helps recock the head for another cross-bridge cycle.
Maple syrup urine disease impairs branched-chain amino-acid catabolism. Leucine, isoleucine and valine require controlled intake; methionine is not one of these branched-chain amino acids.

Genomic imprinting produces parent-of-origin-specific gene expression through epigenetic marking. It differs from mosaicism, which describes genetically different cell populations within one individual.
Verapamil commonly causes constipation through its effects on gastrointestinal smooth muscle. Aliskiren can cause hyperkalaemia rather than the hypokalaemia listed in the distractor.
These drugs inhibit conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone. A reduction in PSA can occur during treatment, but it is a consequence rather than the primary enzyme target.
Descriptive statistics summarise the observed data using tables, graphs and numerical measures. Inferential methods draw conclusions about a wider population from sample observations.
For otherwise comparable sampling, a larger sample reduces standard error. Greater variability or a higher required confidence level generally makes the interval wider.

Insufficient hypothalamic or pituitary stimulation reduces gonadotropin drive to the testes. Low testosterone and impaired sperm production can occur together with low or inappropriately normal LH and FSH.
Pregnancy increases many procoagulant factors, including VII and VIII. Factor XI activity may decrease, illustrating that the changes are not uniform across all clotting factors.
Hormonal therapy, including ACTH in appropriate settings, is used for infantile epileptic spasms associated with West syndrome. Treatment selection also depends on the underlying cause.
Superior oblique primarily intorts the eye and also depresses and abducts it. Its depressive action is particularly useful when the eye is adducted.

Ascending auditory pathways relay through cochlear nuclei and bilateral brainstem circuits, including the superior olivary complex. Fibres then ascend through the lateral lemniscus toward the inferior colliculus.
Phase-contrast optics convert differences in phase caused by variations in optical path into visible intensity differences. This permits viewing many unstained living cells.
Refsum disease impairs peroxisomal alpha-oxidation of phytanic acid. The methyl group near its carboxyl end prevents ordinary initial beta-oxidation until alpha-oxidation processes the substrate.
Adductor pollicis receives the deep branch of the ulnar nerve. Weakness can produce compensatory thumb interphalangeal flexion during the paper-holding manoeuvre known as Froment testing.
Cubitus valgus following a lateral-condyle injury can stretch the ulnar nerve over time. Interosseous weakness impairs finger adduction and abduction.
Unburnt or partially burnt propellant particles can embed in the skin and create tattooing. Soot deposition is a different phenomenon and may be removable from the surface.
A right posterior parietal lesion can disrupt spatial attention to the left side. Neglect is an attentional disorder and is not equivalent to isolated loss of visual acuity.
The normal umbilical cord contains two arteries and one vein. Placental dimensions and weight vary, but the two-vessel-cord statement is the clear abnormality in the listed choices.

An asymmetric optic-nerve lesion can cause a relative afferent pupillary defect. Typical optic neuritis often causes painful eye movements and reduced colour vision; treatment depends on the cause and clinical circumstances.
Fast sodium influx produces phase 0, followed by early transient outward current. Calcium influx supports the plateau, and increased net potassium efflux drives final repolarisation.
Alopecia areata, telogen effluvium and androgenetic alopecia preserve follicular structures sufficiently to be classified as nonscarring. Frontal fibrosing alopecia is a cicatricial disorder.
Minor trauma can tear bridging veins, particularly where cerebral atrophy stretches them. A subdural collection may cause gradually developing headache and neurological symptoms.

The single-breath nitrogen washout method estimates anatomical dead space from the transition between conducting-airway gas and alveolar gas. The Bohr equation instead estimates physiological dead space using carbon dioxide measurements.

The ratio kcat/Km describes catalytic efficiency at low substrate concentrations. It combines turnover once substrate is bound with the enzyme’s effective ability to process substrate; kcat alone is the turnover number.

Most scaphoid blood supply enters distally or at the waist and reaches the proximal pole by retrograde intraosseous flow. A waist fracture can interrupt this supply, making the proximal fragment especially vulnerable to avascular necrosis.

INSM1 is a transcription factor with nuclear staining that supports neuroendocrine differentiation. Synaptophysin is associated with vesicles and chromogranin with secretory granules. The recall abbreviates INSM1 as INSM; its NCAM distractor also contains a CD-number transcription error.

Medullary thyroid carcinoma arises from parafollicular C cells. Its extracellular amyloid is derived from calcitonin-related material. Askanazy and Hurthle are names used for oncocytic follicular cells, so those distractors do not describe the origin of medullary carcinoma.

Conventional fluorescence in situ hybridization detects selected copy-number changes and chromosomal rearrangements using labelled probes. It is not a routine method for detecting individual nucleotide substitutions; sequence-based methods are used for point mutations.

TGF-beta classically inhibits epithelial cell proliferation and helps enforce growth restraint, unlike the listed mitogenic growth factors. Its role is context-dependent: established tumors can exploit TGF-beta signalling to promote invasion and immune evasion.

Pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency impairs conversion of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA. Pyruvate is diverted toward lactate, producing lactic acidosis, often with neurologic disease. This is the best listed answer; congenital lactic acidosis also has other causes.
Heme oxygenase opens the heme ring to produce biliverdin, releasing iron and carbon monoxide. Aminolevulinic acid is instead a precursor in heme synthesis, formed from glycine and succinyl-CoA.

11-beta hydroxylase deficiency reduces cortisol synthesis and increases ACTH, adrenal androgens, and deoxycorticosterone. Androgen excess causes precocious virilization, while the mineralocorticoid effect of deoxycorticosterone causes hypertension.

RNA processing includes capping, methylation and endonucleolytic cleavage. Glycosylation is classically taught as a modification of proteins rather than a standard RNA-processing step. Specialized glycoRNAs exist, so the answer concerns the conventional exam distinction.

Zinc deficiency can impair growth and gonadal maturation, causing delayed puberty and hypogonadism. Other manifestations include impaired wound healing and taste disturbance; the combination is more informative than any single nonspecific symptom.

Tandem mass spectrometry measures multiple amino acids and acylcarnitines from a small blood sample and supports screening for many inborn errors of metabolism. Screening panels vary, and abnormal results require confirmatory testing; it does not detect every metabolic disorder.

Tinea corporis, pityriasis rosea and porokeratosis can produce annular lesions. Urticaria pigmentosa, a form of cutaneous mastocytosis, classically produces pigmented macules or papules that may urticate with rubbing, rather than a typical annular eruption.
Segmental vitiligo often progresses early and then becomes stable, unlike the more variable relapsing course of nonsegmental vitiligo. This is a typical course, not a guarantee for every patient.

Patch testing investigates allergic contact dermatitis; KOH microscopy supports a dermatophyte diagnosis. Biopsy helps evaluate lupus vulgaris, and slit-skin smears can demonstrate acid-fast bacilli in leprosy. These tests support the clinical assessment and have disease-specific sensitivity limits.

Clofazimine can cause red-brown to dark pigmentation of skin and discoloration of body fluids. Its accumulation in tissues also contributes to dryness and gastrointestinal adverse effects. Rifampicin instead classically causes orange-red discoloration of secretions.

Inguinal hernias, particularly indirect inguinal hernias, remain the most common groin hernias in women overall. Femoral hernias have a stronger association with women than men but are less common in absolute number.
Semantic memory stores general knowledge, meanings and concepts. Remembering a particular personal event belongs to episodic memory. Both are forms of declarative memory.

The Mini-Mental State Examination screens cognitive function through tasks involving orientation, registration, attention, recall and language. A screening score supports assessment; it does not by itself establish a diagnosis.

Obsessions are recurrent intrusive thoughts, urges or images, typically experienced as unwanted. They are characteristic of obsessive-compulsive disorder and are not invariably present in schizophrenia. Insight and resistance can vary.

The April 2022 WHO SAGE recommendation allowed one or two HPV vaccine doses for girls aged 9–14 years. This historical recall asks about that recommendation; immunocompromised recipients require a different schedule.
Descriptive statistics summarise observed data using measures such as frequencies, averages and dispersion. Inferential statistics use sample data to draw conclusions about a wider population.

A delayed DPT-containing vaccine series is resumed rather than restarted. The documented first dose still counts, so the next dose is the second dose, followed by completion of the age-appropriate catch-up schedule.
Measles spreads by the airborne route. A patient with suspected or confirmed measles requires airborne precautions and placement in an airborne infection isolation room when available.

In the Indian blood-screening context of this recall, the core mandatory infections are HIV, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, syphilis and malaria. Dengue is not one of those five routine mandatory screening targets.

Prolonged fever, abdominal enlargement and a positive rK39 test suggest visceral leishmaniasis in the appropriate clinical setting. Amphotericin B has antileishmanial activity; its liposomal formulation is an established treatment in India.
